question: To which group of patients should standard precautions be applied?

options.A: Only patients with diagnosed airborne infections
options.B: Only patients presenting with visible bleeding
options.C: All patients regardless of their infectious status
options.D: Only immunocompromised patients in private rooms

explanation: Standard precautions are baseline measures applied to the care of all patients regardless of their diagnosed or presumed infection status. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which of the following body fluids is explicitly excluded from standard precautions unless it contains visible blood?

options.A: Sweat
options.B: Saliva
options.C: Urine
options.D: Semen

explanation: Standard precautions apply to all body fluids, secretions, and excretions except sweat, regardless of whether it contains visible blood. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of understanding the chain of infection in nursing practice?

options.A: To diagnose the specific strain of a bacterial pathogen
options.B: To interrupt the transmission of infectious agents at various links
options.C: To calculate the financial cost of hospital-acquired infections
options.D: To determine the appropriate dosage of broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation: Understanding the chain of infection enables nurses to strategically interrupt pathogen transmission at different links to prevent outbreaks. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which of the following best describes an engineering control in infection control?

options.A: Conducting weekly hand hygiene audits for ward staff
options.B: Providing mandatory educational seminars on malaria prevention
options.C: Using safety-engineered sharps disposal containers
options.D: Isolating a patient diagnosed with active pulmonary tuberculosis

explanation: Engineering controls use physical devices, such as safety-engineered sharps containers, to isolate or remove workplace hazards. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h2)

question: According to the WHO 'My 5 Moments for Hand Hygiene,' when must a nurse clean their hands?

options.A: Only after completing a full 8-hour shift
options.B: Before touching a patient and before clean/aseptic procedures
options.C: Only when family members request it
options.D: Before entering the hospital administrative office

explanation: The WHO moments include before touching a patient and before clean/aseptic procedures, among other critical instances during care delivery. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h3)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water specifically required over alcohol-based hand rubs?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled or dirty
options.B: Whenever a nurse enters a patient room quickly
options.C: Only at the beginning of a nursing shift
options.D: When the nurse is wearing sterile gloves

explanation: Handwashing with soap and water is mandatory when hands are visibly soiled, dirty, or contaminated with organic matter. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is the typical correct sequence for donning personal protective equipment (PPE)?

options.A: Gloves, gown, mask, eye protection
options.B: Gown, mask or respirator, eye protection, gloves
options.C: Eye protection, gloves, gown, mask
options.D: Mask, gloves, gown, eye protection

explanation: The standard donning sequence starts with the gown, followed by the mask or respirator, eye protection, and gloves last. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which of the following statements regarding medical gloves and hand hygiene is true?

options.A: Gloves eliminate the need for hand hygiene entirely.
options.B: Hand hygiene must be performed immediately after removing gloves.
options.C: Gloves should be washed with soap and water between patients for reuse.
options.D: Alcohol rub can be applied while gloves are still on the hands.

explanation: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene, and hands must always be cleaned immediately after removing gloves to eliminate micro-organisms. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h4)

question: What is the recommended action regarding used needles and syringes after an injection?

options.A: Recap the needle immediately using both hands for safety
options.B: Place the uncapped needle and syringe directly into a puncture-resistant safety box
options.C: Break the needle off before throwing it in a standard waste bin
options.D: Store the needle in your pocket until the end of the shift

explanation: Used needles should not be recapped; instead, they must be disposed of uncapped directly into a puncture-resistant safety box. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h5)

question: At what capacity should a sharps disposal box be sealed and replaced?

options.A: When it is completely overflowing
options.B: Once every month regardless of fill level
options.C: When it reaches the designated three-quarters fill line
options.D: As soon as the first needle is dropped inside

explanation: Safety boxes should never be overfilled; they must be sealed and replaced when they reach the three-quarters full mark. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h5)

question: What should a person do if they do not have a tissue when about to cough or sneeze?

options.A: Cough directly into their bare hands
options.B: Cough into their inner elbow
options.C: Turn around and cough openly into the air
options.D: Cover their mouth with a medical glove and reuse it

explanation: If a tissue is unavailable, coughing or sneezing into the inner elbow prevents hands from becoming contaminated with respiratory droplets. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which type of respiratory protection is required when caring for a patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: A standard cloth face covering
options.B: A surgical ear-loop mask
options.C: An N95 or higher-level respirator
options.D: No mask is necessary if standing two meters away

explanation: Airborne pathogens like tuberculosis require high-efficiency respirators such as N95 masks to protect healthcare personnel from inhaling small droplet nuclei. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is the primary objective of cleaning a surface before applying a chemical disinfectant?

options.A: To make the surface smell pleasant for the patient
options.B: To remove visible dirt and organic matter that can deactivate disinfectants
options.C: To polish the furniture to a high shine
options.D: To reduce the drying time of the chemical solution

explanation: Removing organic matter through cleaning is essential because soil and protein can shield microorganisms and neutralize chemical disinfectants. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h7)

question: How should environmental surfaces in a hospital ward generally be cleaned to prevent spreading contamination?

options.A: From the dirtiest areas to the cleanest areas
options.B: In a random pattern across the entire room
options.C: From the cleanest areas to the dirtiest areas
options.D: Only when the ward manager inspects the unit

explanation: Cleaning should always progress methodically from the cleanest areas to the dirtiest areas to avoid transferring heavy contamination to clean zones. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h7)

question: How should reusable non-critical patient care equipment, such as a blood pressure cuff, be managed between patients?

options.A: It should be stored in the supply room for one week without cleaning.
options.B: It must be cleaned and disinfected between each patient use.
options.C: It only needs to be wiped down at the end of the nursing shift.
options.D: It requires high-level heat sterilization before every application.

explanation: Reusable patient care equipment touching intact skin must be properly cleaned and disinfected between every patient use to prevent cross-infection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h8)

question: What is the correct procedure for handling soiled linen in a hospital ward?

options.A: Shake the linen vigorously to remove dust before bagging
options.B: Rinse the soiled linen in the patient sink immediately
options.C: Place the linen directly into a leak-proof laundry bag with minimum agitation
options.D: Carry the linen openly in your arms to the laundry chute

explanation: Soiled linen should be handled with minimum agitation and placed directly into leak-proof bags at the point of use to prevent spreading pathogens. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h8)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after sustaining a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Squeeze the wound tightly to force out contaminated blood
options.B: Wash the affected skin site immediately with soap and clean water
options.C: Apply an antiseptic alcohol tincture and cover with a tight bandage
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to report it before cleaning

explanation: The immediate action is to wash the puncture site with soap and water; scrubbing or aggressive squeezing should be avoided as it can increase tissue damage. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h9)

question: Why is timely reporting of a needle-stick injury critical in healthcare settings?

options.A: To ensure the nurse is immediately suspended from clinical duties
options.B: To facilitate prompt risk assessment and timely initiation of Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP)
options.C: To allow ward management to penalize the staff member for carelessness
options.D: To order routine disinfection of the entire hospital floor

explanation: Prompt reporting allows for immediate risk evaluation and timely initiation of PEP, which is vital for preventing infections like HIV following exposure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h9)

question: What is a major challenge frequently encountered when implementing standard precautions in Nigerian community health settings?

options.A: An absolute surplus of disposable PPE and safety boxes
options.B: Resource limitations, irregular water supply, and supply shortages
options.C: The complete absence of infectious diseases in rural populations
options.D: Patients refusing all forms of physical examination

explanation: Community health facilities in resource-constrained settings often struggle with irregular water supplies and shortages of consumable infection control items. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h10)

question: What role do nurses commonly play in promoting infection prevention within local community health centers?

options.A: Acting as change agents who demonstrate correct practices and advocate for safety
options.B: Ignoring guidelines until luxury medical equipment is imported
options.C: Strictly isolating all patients regardless of their symptoms
options.D: Avoiding clinical procedures to eliminate all occupational risks

explanation: Nurses act as vital local change agents, educating staff, demonstrating safe techniques, and advocating for continuous infection control improvements. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T9#GNS313_U2_T9_h10)
